caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: DANDI:001277
attempts.paper_title: MHz compression of pulse packets facilitates remote focusing of electroporation
attempts.entry_title: Remote focusing of electroporation by MHz pulse packets (Silkuniene et al. 2025)
attempts.summary: The paper's central finding held in this data: MHz pulse packets focused electroporation at the centre of the electrode array in both cell lines, killing stayed there, and one burst gave the sharpest spot, about 1.1 mm wide. The 40-fold excess of central over near-electrode uptake was met only for some choices of background footprint, which the paper does not name. Narrowing with packet rate could not be tested, as the intermediate rates are not deposited. Narrowing with longer pulses held only when two wells were left out, one for the breadth under test, and raised electrodes did not clearly weaken the centre. The electroporation spot was narrower than the killing spot; the paper reports it slightly larger.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Silkuniene, Silkunas, Pakhomova, Semenov and Pakhomov (2025) on dandisets 001047, 001276, 001277 and 001284, which hold whole-well images of cell monolayers stained with YO-PRO-1, propidium and Hoechst after CANCAN pulse exposures. It measures dye uptake along the diagonals of the four-electrode array for the raised-electrode and cell-killing series (001284), the pulse-duration series (001277) and the burst-number series (001276), with the packet-rate claims that its 1-Hz, 0.2-MHz and control wells allow. The 1-kHz and 10-kHz wells of Figures 3 and 4 are in none of the dandisets; 001047 holds images from a smaller array.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Silkuniene et al. (2025) from dandisets 001047, 001276, 001277 and 001284
Findings of the earlier attempt silkuniene-2025-03 on DANDI:001277, checked again

outcomes.statement: In the simulation, 7.2 kV on one electrode gives 3.3 kV/cm in the centre of the array and 9.4 and 13.5 kV/cm at 6 and 7 mm from the centre toward the active electrode.
outcomes.quote: Specifically, 7.2 kV applied to one electrode produced the electric field of 3.3 kV/cm in the center, and 9.4 and 13.5 kV/cm at 6 and 7 mm from the center towards the active electrode, respectively
outcomes.notes: None of the four dandisets holds the Sim4Life field maps; every file is a fluorescence image of a well (metadata of all 329 files listed in the notebook). The paper does not deposit them.

outcomes.statement: With packets at the maximum rate, heating followed the field and was largest near the electrodes; after 2 bursts it was confined to about 2 mm next to the electrodes and could exceed 30 C but not 44 C; after 6 bursts it spread further, exceeding 30 C even near the centre, yet never exceeded 44 C.
outcomes.quote: With 2 bursts ( Fig. 2A ), heating was restricted to an approximately 2-mm zone next to electrodes, where it could reach over 30 °C but did not exceed 44 °C. With 6 bursts ( Fig. 2B ), heating was more widespread ... Temperature could exceed 30 °C even near the center of the array, but did not exceed 44 °C even near the electrodes.
outcomes.notes: No thermochromic film image or movie is in any of the four dandisets; every file is a fluorescence image of a cell monolayer.

outcomes.statement: Every CANCAN protocol enhanced electroporation at the array centre, while in the control (a single unipolar pulse per packet) YP uptake decreased gradually toward the centre.
outcomes.quote: All CANCAN protocols visibly enhanced electroporation at the center of the array, in contrast to its gradual decrease toward the center in the control ( Fig. 3A ).
outcomes.notes: What the answer changed. The verified outcome was blocked, as the claims file listed 001047 only, whose files all state a 3.8-mm array and a 3.2-kV first pulse. The reader found that by the paper the 0.2-MHz condition of the series is the protocol of the 2-burst CT26 group of Fig. 7 and added 001276, with the criterion judging the claim on the rates held and capping it at partial. Tested now on 001276, under the ROI readings, the footprint readings (i) to (iv) of the amended O1, pooling and side. At 0.2 MHz the centre exceeds YP at 4 mm by a gap in 24 of 24 combinations (t-test p 0.0003 to 0.0053); at 1 Hz in 21 of 24 (all 8 under pooling b, 13 of 16 under pooling a; t-test p 0.062 to 0.195). The control centre (2237 to 2301 a.u.) is not below YP at 4, 6 and 7 mm by a gap in any of the 24 (YP at 4 mm 1749 to 2267 a.u.; t-test p 0.25 to 0.98), and the 13 August 2024 wells give the same. 001047 holds none of these wells, and no dandiset holds the 1-kHz or 10-kHz wells. The CANCAN part holds at 0.2 MHz in every reading and at 1 Hz in most (3 of 16 fail under pooling a), and the control part fails, so the claim holds in part. Changed from blocked after the verifier agreed in round 3.
deviations: The 1-Hz CANCAN group has 2 wells and the control group 4, where the paper reports n = 3 per rate and n = 5 controls; all wells are used, and the 13 August 2024 wells, the one date with all three conditions, are shown as a second set.

outcomes.statement: Raising the packet rate from 1 Hz to 0.2 MHz suppressed electroporation better both near the electrodes (diagonal profile) and at the perimeter between electrodes (profile parallel to the sides).
outcomes.quote: The most conspicuous effect of increasing the packet rate from 1 Hz to 0.208333 MHz (abbreviated to 0.2 MHz below and in figure legends) was better suppression of electroporation both near electrodes ( Fig. 3B ) and at the perimeter between electrodes ( Fig. 3C ).
outcomes.notes: What the answer changed. The verified outcome was blocked, as the claims file listed 001047 only; the reader added 001276 (see fig3a-centre-enhanced). The perimeter part is tested on ROIs placed by code on the whole-well images along the lines through the centre parallel to the sides (6 mm under whole-mm ROIs and 6.09 mm under contiguous ROIs, the last inside the square; the criterion's two perimeter readings are the same ROIs here). Over the footprint readings (i) to (iv), YP at 0.2 MHz is 2.5 to 6.6% of that at 1 Hz at 6 mm, 4.3 to 11.9% at 7 mm and 6.8 to 16.4% at the perimeter (t-test p at most 0.0095, 0.0193 and 0.0048). By the graph rule it is lower by a gap in 24 of 24 combinations at the perimeter, 23 of 24 at 6 mm and 17 of 24 at 7 mm; every failure is under pooling (a) on the left side (40 of 48 hold under pooling a, 24 of 24 under pooling b). The 13 August 2024 wells give 39 of 48 and 24 of 24. The verified outcome is kept and a change to reproduced, resting on the pooling, is proposed; the verifier did not agree in round 3 (proposed).
deviations: The ROIs parallel to the sides are placed by code on the whole-well images, from the centre to the middle of each side (cancan.parallel_profiles); the paper's Fig. 3C ROIs were measured on one set only and their positions are not given.
The 1-Hz group has 2 wells, where the paper reports n = 3.

Proposed as an assumption, pooling (b) of O2 decides where the readings differ. The Fig. 4A legend says "measurements in 4 diagonal directions from the center were pooled" for the near-electrode values of the same experiments (Fig. 4B); Fig. 3B plots profiles from -x to x (pooling a), under which one side fails at 7 mm.

proposed.reason: Tested on 001276 after the reader's answer. Under pooling (b), the reading the Fig. 4A legend gives for the near-electrode values of these experiments, 0.2 MHz is below 1 Hz by a gap at 6 mm, 7 mm and the perimeter under every footprint and ROI reading (24 of 24); under pooling (a) the left side at 7 mm fails in 7 of 8 combinations, where one of the two 1-Hz wells is low. The outcome rests on pooling (b), an assumption. The verifier did not agree in round 3 and would give blocked (methods_underspecified). In its words, the Fig. 4A legend describes the Fig. 4B near-electrode values, while this claim cites Fig. 3B, whose legend says "Measurements in two diagonals were averaged and considered as one experiment", plotted from -x to x, as Methods 2.5 does, so the paper supports pooling (a), and (b) was picked after (a) had failed. Under pooling (a) the outcome also depends on the footprint (only footprint i with whole-mm ROIs passes), which under the claims-file rule gives a block, and the failures come from the graph rule applied to two 1-Hz wells, as every t-test gives p of 0.019 or less. The verified outcome is kept; whether O2 leaves the pooling open for this claim is asked of a reader.

outcomes.statement: The decline of YP emission from the centre was bell-shaped and fitted a Lorentzian function over -4 to 4 mm nearly perfectly (R > 0.9, p < 0.001) for every packet rate.
outcomes.quote: The fit correlation with data in the −4 to 4 mm radius was nearly perfect (R>0.9, p<0.001).

statistics.about: correlation of the Lorentzian fit with the data, -4 to 4 mm
significance of each YP fit in Figures 3, 5 and 6 (Methods 2.5)

outcomes.notes: What the answer changed. The verified outcome was blocked, as the claims file listed 001047 only; the reader added 001276 and wrote that with only some rates held the claim is at most partially reproduced. Over the footprint readings (i) to (iv), the ROI readings, pooling, both R readings and both directions, R is 0.946 to 0.997 with the largest p 1.2e-04 (62 of 64 combinations below 1e-4); the 13 August 2024 wells give R 0.946 to 0.994. The 1-kHz and 10-kHz wells are in no dandiset. At the two rates held the fit holds under every reading, and the criterion allows at most partial. Changed from blocked after the verifier agreed in round 3.

outcomes.statement: Beyond the fitted range, the data deviated from the Lorentzian fit less as the packet rate increased.
outcomes.quote: The deviation of experimental data from the fits at larger distances from the center diminished with increasing the packet repetition rate, highlighting better suppression of the off-target electroporation.
outcomes.notes: The reader's answer of 2026-11-20 kept this claim on DANDI:001047 only, as a trend over the packet rates cannot be tested with two rates; 001047 holds no images from the paper's array, and no dandiset holds the 1-kHz or 10-kHz wells. As a variant that decides nothing, on the two rates of 001276 the data lie above the fit beyond 4 mm by 24.6 to 35.9% of the fitted peak at 1 Hz and 1.1 to 4.4% at 0.2 MHz (footprint readings i to iv).

outcomes.statement: At 0.2 MHz, YP uptake at the centre was 40 times that near the electrodes, despite the field there being about 4 times weaker (3.3 against about 14 kV/cm).
outcomes.quote: Now, by increasing the packet repetition rate to 0.2 MHz, we achieved a 40-fold difference ( Fig. 4B ), despite using a bigger array with larger reduction of the electric field from electrodes to the center.
outcomes.notes: What the answers changed. The verified outcome was blocked, as the claims file listed 001047 only; the reader added 001276 (first answer) and made the background footprint an open reading, the claim holding when the ratio is in range under one combination and resting on the footprint that gives it (second answer). At 6 mm the ratio of means is 33.4 to 39.4 with footprint (i), 31.2 to 36.3 with (ii), 39.9 to 48.8 with (iii) and 75.0 to 114.9 with (iv); at 7 mm every footprint gives 10.6 to 29.5. The mean of per-well ratios is unstable, as with a fixed footprint some wells' near-electrode values fall below zero. The darkest footprint, used before the answer, gives a 6-mm ratio of means of 26.7 to 30.4 and a mean of ratios of 35.4 to 52.0. On the 13 August 2024 wells (n = 3) 6 of 48 combinations are inside. The fields are the paper's simulation and are not tested. The ratio is inside 36 to 44 under 10 of 48 combinations, all at 6 mm. The first the criterion lists (footprint i, pooling a, 6 mm, ratio of means, whole-mm ROIs) gives 39.4 on the left side and 33.4 on the right; under pooling (b), footprint (iii) at 6 mm gives 43.9 and 43.2 over the ROI readings. The evidence is weak: the footprint choice alone moves the 6-mm ratio of means from 31.2 to 114.9, across the whole band, and the darkest footprint gives no ratio of means in range. Changed from blocked after the verifier agreed in round 3; the outcome rests on the footprint.
deviations: Assumed, the footprint that gives the background is the one under which the ratio is in range (claims file O1 and the criterion, as amended on 2026-11-20); every combination is shown.

outcomes.statement: YP uptake at the array centre showed no significant effect of packet rate.
outcomes.quote: YP intensity in the center showed no significant effect of the packet rate ( t -test with Bonferroni correction, Fig. 4B ).
outcomes.notes: The packet-rate series is not in DANDI:001047, and no dandiset holds the 1-kHz and 10-kHz wells. The reader's answer of 2026-11-20 kept the claim on 001047 only, as the test is a family over the rates, which the two rates of 001276 cannot give.

outcomes.statement: In contrast to the centre, YP uptake at 6 and 7 mm from the centre (1.65 and 0.65 mm from the electrodes) declined steeply as the packet rate increased.
outcomes.quote: It contrasted with a steep, packet rate-dependent decline of YP uptake at 6 and 7 mm from the center (i.e., 1.65 and 0.65 mm from electrodes).
outcomes.notes: The packet-rate series is not in DANDI:001047, and no dandiset holds the 1-kHz and 10-kHz wells. The reader's answer of 2026-11-20 kept the claim on 001047 only, as a power-law trend over the rates cannot be fitted to two rates.

outcomes.statement: Higher packet rates focused electroporation into a smaller spot; the FWHM fell from about 4 mm at 1 Hz to about 2 mm at 1 kHz, 10 kHz and 0.2 MHz (p = 0.03, 0.02 and 0.09 against 1 Hz), and could be under 15% of the gap between electrodes.
outcomes.quote: FWHM decreased from ~4 mm at 1 Hz to ~2 mm at 1 kHz, 10 kHz, and 0.2 MHz packet rates (p = 0.03; 0.02, and 0.09, respectively; t -test with Bonferroni correction).
outcomes.notes: The packet-rate series is not in DANDI:001047, and no dandiset holds the 1-kHz and 10-kHz wells the claim's values and tests rest on. The reader's answer of 2026-11-20 kept the claim on 001047 only.

outcomes.statement: FWHM fell logarithmically with packet rate from 1 Hz to 10 kHz (R = 0.77, p < 0.001; n = 15), with no further narrowing from 10 kHz to 0.2 MHz.
outcomes.quote: FWHM decrease followed the logarithmic dependence from 1 Hz to 10 kHz (correlation coefficient R = 0.77, p<0.001), but there was no further focality increase when the packet rate increased from 10 kHz to 0.2 MHz.

statistics.about: log fit of FWHM against packet rate, 1 Hz to 10 kHz
slope of the log fit (Fig. 4C legend)

outcomes.notes: Depends on fig4c-fwhm-falls-with-rate; the series is in no dandiset. The reader's answer of 2026-11-20 kept the claim on 001047 only.

outcomes.statement: Since with MHz-CANCAN there was practically no YP staining near electrodes (a finding the text cites to Figure 4), the only clear effect of raising the electrodes 1 or 2 mm above the monolayer was a weakening of electroporation in the central spot.
outcomes.quote: With MHz-CANCAN (CT26 cells, 2 bursts (x4), Fig. 4 ), there was practically no YP staining near electrodes to start with, so the only clear effect of raising electrodes was the weakening of electroporation in the central spot.
outcomes.notes: With all wells, mean centre YP is 48.7% (1 mm, n = 11) and 28.9% (2 mm, n = 11) of the 0-mm value (n = 12, s.e. 24.3%). The 2-mm drop exceeds the error bars by the paper's graph rule, the 1-mm drop does not; Student's t-tests p = 0.079 and 0.028, Bonferroni 0.158 and 0.056. With the August 2024 wells alone (7, 6 and 7, the paper's n = 6 to 7), the centre is 68.2% and 49.0% of the August 0-mm mean and neither drop exceeds the error bars (Bonferroni p = 0.558 and 0.356). The criterion needs both drops, which neither set gives. YP at 6 and 7 mm is 1.5 to 7.4% of the 0-mm centre at every elevation with all wells (2.0 to 12.7% in the August wells). In the October 2024 wells alone (5, 5 and 4 wells) the centre is 121.8% of the all-wells 0-mm mean at 0 mm and 38.0% and 7.1% of it at 1 and 2 mm. What the second answer changed (2026-11-20): the background footprint is now an open reading, (i) to (iv) the footprint at the same position in every well, and the claim was run under each. The outcome is the same under each: with all wells the 1-mm centre is 48.2 to 48.5% of the 0-mm mean (no gap) and the 2-mm centre 28.2 to 28.5% (gap); with the August wells neither drop has a gap.
deviations: The dandiset holds 12, 11 and 11 YP wells at 0, 1 and 2 mm, where the paper reports n = 6 to 7; all were used, as the paper does not say which it used. The August 2024 batch (7, 6 and 7 wells) matches the paper's n and is shown as a second reading for every Fig. 5 YP claim.

In 23 of 34 001284 wells the footprints could not be found (the array is raised, or the footprints are faint), and the centre is the centre of the central YP spot (an assumption; in wells where both are known they are 0.36 mm apart, median).

outcomes.statement: With MHz-CANCAN, cell killing (propidium uptake 2 h after exposure) was produced at the centre of the array with negligible effect near the electrodes.
outcomes.quote: The principal accomplishment of this study is the selective electroporation and cell killing at a remote location with negligible effect near electrodes.
outcomes.notes: At 0 mm (n = 5) centre Pr is 1188 +/- 339 a.u. and Pr at 6 and 7 mm 8.2 to 16.5 a.u. (0.7 to 1.4% of the centre), below the centre by more than the error bars under both ROI readings (t-test p = 0.008 to 0.009; paired p = 0.025). At 1 mm the gap holds (about 13% of the centre); at 2 mm the centre Pr is 23 a.u. and it does not. What the second answer changed (2026-11-20): the background footprint is now an open reading, (i) to (iv) the footprint at the same position in every well, and the claim was run under each. The gaps hold under each and both ROI readings, Pr at 6 and 7 mm being -0.2 to 1.2% of the centre (t-test p 0.008 to 0.009).
deviations: The Pr images share the frame of the YP image of the same well (spot centres 0.05 to 0.16 mm apart at 0 mm); the array geometry of a well is taken from whichever of its images shows the footprints, otherwise from the YP spot.

outcomes.statement: The central spot of YP staining (electroporation) was only slightly larger than the spot of Pr staining (cell killing).
outcomes.quote: Somewhat unexpectedly, the central spot of YP staining (electroporation) was just slightly larger than the spot of Pr staining (cell killing; Fig 5A and B ).
outcomes.notes: At 0 mm the Lorentzian FWHM of mean YP is 1.69 to 1.75 mm and the Gaussian FWHM (2.4 sigma) of mean Pr 2.29 to 2.34 mm, a ratio of 0.74 to 0.75 under every reading (0.66 to 0.67 with only the 5 YP wells that also have a Pr image; 0.75 to 0.76 with 2.355 sigma). By FWHM the YP spot is narrower than the Pr spot. With the 7 August YP wells, the paper's n, the ratio is 0.82 to 0.83. The tails differ the other way (fig5b-reversible-beyond-2mm), so a spot size read from the tails, not the FWHM the criterion uses, could rank them differently. What the second answer changed (2026-11-20): the background footprint is now an open reading, (i) to (iv) the footprint at the same position in every well, and the claim was run under each. The ratio is 0.723 to 0.750 with all YP wells, outside both ranges in all 16 combinations.
deviations: All 12 YP wells at 0 mm are used against the 5 Pr wells; the 5 matched wells are shown.

outcomes.statement: Pr intensity declined from the peak as a Gaussian and YP as a Lorentzian; in the left panel of Figure 5B the R2 was 0.92 (Lorentzian) against 0.96 (Gaussian) for Pr, and 0.98 against 0.95 for YP, fitted from -5 to 5 mm with p < 0.0001.
outcomes.quote: For Pr data in the left panel of Fig. 5B , the coefficient of determination increased from 0.92 for Lorentzian fit to 0.96 for Gaussian fit. YP data showed the opposite trend, with the coefficients of 0.98 and 0.95 for Lorentzian and Gaussian fits, respectively (for all these fits, the fitted region was from −5 to 5 mm, p<0.0001).
outcomes.notes: R2 over -5 to 5 mm (whole-mm ROIs, two diagonals averaged, given as measured) under all four readings: Pr Lorentzian 0.937 to 0.960, Pr Gaussian 0.984 to 0.998, YP Lorentzian 0.975 to 0.993, YP Gaussian 0.960 to 0.979; both orderings hold under every reading, and every F test p is below 1.1e-06. With the 7 August YP wells, YP R2 is 0.976 to 0.995 (Lorentzian) and 0.947 to 0.966 (Gaussian), the Lorentzian above under every reading. What the second answer changed (2026-11-20): the background footprint is now an open reading, (i) to (iv) the footprint at the same position in every well, and the claim was run under each. R2 is 0.933 to 0.959 and 0.984 to 0.998 for Pr and 0.973 to 0.993 and 0.962 to 0.984 for YP, within tolerance with both orderings holding; the largest F-test p is 1.4e-06.

outcomes.statement: The Lorentzian YP profile and the Gaussian Pr profile differ mainly in the tails, where YP is broader, marking an area of predominantly reversible electroporation that starts about 2 mm from the centre.
outcomes.quote: The difference between the fits is primarily in the tails, which are broader in Lorentzian distribution compared to Gaussian. This difference highlights the area of predominantly reversible electroporation, which extends outwards starting at about 2 mm from the center.
outcomes.notes: Reading (b), the fitted curves, gives 2.08 mm (whole-mm ROIs) and 2.11 mm (contiguous ROIs), inside 1.8 to 2.2 mm. Reading (a), the data by the graph rule, gives 3.0 mm and 2.84 mm (3.25 and 2.44 mm on the two sides), outside it. The criterion needs one reading. The value given is reading (b) with whole-mm ROIs, the first ROI reading the claims file lists, as reading (a) does not match. With the four half-diagonals pooled (O2 reading b), reading (b) gives 2.06 and 2.09 mm and reading (a) 3.00 and 2.84 mm. With the 7 August YP wells, reading (b) gives 1.78 to 1.83 mm. What the second answer changed (2026-11-20): the background footprint is now an open reading, (i) to (iv) the footprint at the same position in every well, and the claim was run under each. Reading (b) gives 2.04 to 2.15 mm in all 16 combinations of ROI reading and pooling; reading (a) 2.84 to 3.50 mm.

outcomes.statement: In the central spot cells showed bright nuclear YP staining, indicating irreversible damage, while farther out reversibly electroporated cells were weakly stained with less contrast between nucleus and cytoplasm; cells inside the electrode footprint were unstained though present (Hoechst).
outcomes.quote: Indeed, a closer examination of the central spot confirmed bright YP staining of cell nuclei ( Fig. 5C , zone 1), which is indicative of the irreversible membrane damage and cell death. Reversible electroporation is distinguished by a much weaker YP staining and smaller difference in staining of the nucleus and cytoplasm, such as in zones 2 and 3 in Fig. 5C .
outcomes.notes: Intensity part holds in 12 of 12 wells at 0 mm; means 1607.5 a.u. (zone 1), 140.2 or 86.1 (zone 2, readings a and b), 320.8 (zone 3) and 10.5 (footprints). Footprint part holds in 5 of 5 wells with a 2-h Hoechst image; the footprint Hoechst signal is 1.21 to 1.57 of the way from the camera offset to the well median. The nuclear part could not be tested; every 001284 file is a 4x whole-well image, and the high-resolution images of Fig. 5C are not deposited.
deviations: Cells counted as present when the footprint Hoechst mean is at least half-way from the camera offset (0.1st percentile of the image) to the well median, a standard choice; the paper names no reference level.

outcomes.statement: The central YP peak was highest for 900-ns pulses, but not significantly different from 300- or 600-ns pulses.
outcomes.quote: The central peak of YP uptake was higher for 900-ns pulses, but the difference from the other two pulse durations was not statistically significant (CT26 cells, 2 bursts (x4), Fig. 6B ).
outcomes.notes: Mean centre YP 538, 800 and 891 a.u. for 300, 600 and 900 ns (n = 5 each); 900 against 300 ns p = 0.288 (Bonferroni 0.576, Cohen's d 0.72), against 600 ns p = 0.801 (Bonferroni 1.0); ANOVA p = 0.506. With all seven 600-ns wells, 900 ns is still highest and nothing is significant (ANOVA p = 0.470), and the same holds with only B2 left out (ANOVA p = 0.481). Over the 21 ways of choosing five of the seven 600-ns wells, 900 ns is highest with no corrected p below 0.05 in 20; in the other, 900 ns is not the highest.
deviations: Two 600-ns wells (P1-20240926-B2 and B3) are left out in the main reading; see fig6d-longer-pulses-sharper-peak. The outcome is the same with both, and with B2 alone, left in.

outcomes.statement: Normalized to the central peak, the sideways decline of YP was similar for the three pulse durations.
outcomes.quote: When the peak YP emission was taken as 100%, its decline sideways was similar for the three tested pulse durations ( Fig. 6C ).
outcomes.notes: By the graph rule, durations differ by more than the error bars at some distances under every reading; 5 to 20 distance and pair combinations with n = 5 per duration (mostly 300 ns above 600 or 900 ns at 1 to 3 mm, for example 20.2% against 12.3% of the peak at 2 mm), and 2 to 10 with all seven 600-ns wells (mostly 300 against 900 ns; under contiguous ROIs also 600 against 900 ns at +/-0.81 mm). The broader 300-ns peak is the effect the paper reports in Fig. 6D, so the paper's "similar" and its Fig. 6D finding pull against each other. What the second answer changed (2026-11-20): the background footprint is now an open reading, (i) to (iv) the footprint at the same position in every well, and the claim was run under each. Durations differ by a gap at some distance under every reading (4 to 26 distance and pair combinations with n = 5, 2 to 16 with all seven 600-ns wells).

outcomes.statement: Fitted per experiment, the FWHM of the central YP peak decreases with pulse duration from 300 to 900 ns, with a trend slope different from zero (p = 0.003).
outcomes.quote: However, a more detailed analysis based on fitting of individual experiments (as described in 3.1 ) revealed significant sharpening of the central peak when packets were built from 600- and 900-ns pulses ( Fig. 6D ). The slope coefficient of the logarithmic fit of the data was different from zero at p = 0.003 (one sample, 2-sided t -test).

statistics.about: slope of FWHM against pulse duration

outcomes.notes: With only P1-20240926-B2 left out (n = 6 at 600 ns), the well choice the data support, the slopes are negative with p = 0.51 to 0.77 on experiments and 0.63 to 0.83 on group means, and the 600-ns mean FWHM (2.48 mm) is above the 300-ns mean (2.15 mm). With all seven 600-ns wells p = 0.86 to 0.99. B3 is left out of the main cells to give n = 5, but the only thing that sets it apart is its broad profile, the quantity under test: its YP spot is 0.33 mm from the array centre, its profile is highest at the centre and its centre value (748 a.u.) is inside the range of the other 600-ns wells, while YP at 3 mm is 46% of its centre against 5 to 13% in the other wells of 001277. With B2 and B3 left out (mean FWHM 2.15, 1.87 and 1.75 mm for 300, 600 and 900 ns, whole-mm ROIs, 4-mm range) the slope on experiments has p = 0.0008 to 0.0058 (paper 0.003) and on group means 0.048 to 0.165; over the 21 ways of choosing five of the seven 600-ns wells the criterion holds only for that choice, and in the other 20 the largest p is 0.79 to 0.98. The criterion needs p < 0.05 under every reading, so the claim is not reproduced, on per-experiment points and on group means. Changed from reproduced (assumed) after the verifier agreed in round 3. What the second answer changed (2026-11-20): the background footprint is now an open reading, (i) to (iv) the footprint at the same position in every well, and the claim was run under each. With the main wells every slope on experiments is negative with p = 0.0003 to 0.0465 (on group means 0.000 to 0.154); with only B2 left out p = 0.45 to 0.88; with all seven wells 0.84 to 0.98 (cell 77). The outcome is as it was.
deviations: Per-experiment FWHM values are the main regression points (claims file O4 reading a). The text says the analysis was "based on fitting of individual experiments" (Results 3.3), and Fig. 4C fits individual experiments (n = 15). Group means give the same outcome.

The dandiset labels seven wells 600 ns, where the paper reports n = 5 (Fig. 6 legend). Plates P2 and P3 hold two wells of each duration, and plate P1 one 300-ns, one 900-ns, a sham and three 600-ns wells (A3, B2, B3). The outcome is decided with only B2 left out, as its YP spot is 5.39 mm from the array centre, against at most 1.21 mm in every other 0.2-MHz CANCAN well with footprints. The main cells also leave out B3 to give n = 5; B3 differs from the other wells of 001277 only in its broad profile, the quantity under test, so that choice is not independent of the result. All seven, the six without B2, and all 21 subsets of five, are shown.

findings.statement: DANDI:001047, which cites the paper, holds images from a 3.8-mm array with a 3.2-kV first pulse (per-file metadata and images), not the paper's 15.3-mm array with 7.2-kV pulses. Of the packet-rate series of Figures 3 and 4 (1 Hz to 0.2 MHz) only the 1-Hz, 0.2-MHz and control wells are deposited, in 001276; the 1-kHz and 10-kHz wells are in none of the four dandisets, and neither are the field simulation (Fig. 1), the thermochromic film images (Fig. 2) or the high-resolution images of Fig. 5C. Seven of the paper's claims cannot be tested.

DANDI:001276 holds CT26 and CHO wells exposed at a 1-Hz packet rate and control wells, which its description (0.2 MHz, 1 to 6 bursts) does not mention and whose role in the paper is not stated; by the paper's protocol they fit the packet-rate series of Figures 3 and 4, and a reader's answer assigns four of its claims to them. The CT26 wells at 2 bursts (x4) hold CANCAN at 1 Hz (n = 2) and 0.2 MHz (n = 6) and controls (n = 4), with all three conditions on 13 August 2024.

Several groups hold more wells than the paper reports. 001284 has 12, 11 and 11 YP wells at 0, 1 and 2 mm (paper n = 6 to 7); 001276 has 5, 8, 7 and 8 CHO wells at 1, 2, 4 and 6 bursts (paper n = 4) and 6 CT26 wells at 2 bursts (paper n = 3 to 5); 001277 has 7 wells labelled 600 ns (paper n = 5). In 001284 the August 2024 YP wells (7, 6 and 7) match the paper's YP n and the October 2024 wells (5, 5 and 4) its Pr n. Which wells the paper used is not recorded.

In 001277, wells P1-20240926-B2 and B3 are labelled 600-ns 0.2-MHz CANCAN. In B2 the YP spot is 5.39 mm from the array centre, against at most 1.21 mm in every other 0.2-MHz CANCAN well with footprints; B3 has its YP maximum at the centre, but YP at 3 and 5 mm is 46% and 35% of the centre, against at most 13% and 9% in the other wells of 001277. The label or the exposure of these two wells may differ from the description.

Every 001277 file states "9 packets of pulses delivered at 0.2MHz", whatever the pulse duration (counts by duration in the notebook's data check), where the dandiset description and the paper give 18, 9 and 6 packets for 300, 600 and 900 ns. In 001284, the pre-exposure Hoechst files of wells P1-20241002-B2 and P2-20241004-B1 state 900-ns pulses, while the other files of these wells state 600 ns.
The FITC image of 001284 well P1-20240828-A3 (11 MB) is 98% zero pixels, and the pre-exposure DAPI file of 001276 well P1-20240821-A2 holds only zeros.
The Cy3-DAPI image of 001277 well P2-20240925-B3 is deposited twice (sub-P2-20240925-B3_image.nwb and sub-P2-20240925-B3_obj-w6fqmq_image.nwb, identical size and data).

The dandiset descriptions and files give a 10-mm inter-electrode distance, which matches none of the distances the paper gives (15.3 mm between needle edges along a diagonal, 12.8 mm between needle centres along a side, as the electrode footprints in the images confirm).

In 001277 the OME metadata, which only the 13 Cy3-DAPI files carry, give 12 significant bits per pixel, but these files hold values far above 4095 (maxima in the central 2000 x 2000 pixels 8926 to 25073 in the Cy3 channel and 19419 to 65535 in the DAPI channel), so the stored values are not 12-bit camera counts. The ImageSeries unit is "n.a." in all 49 files and no scaling is described; the FITC and DAPI files carry no OME metadata.

The 001277 files give no electrode positions, ROI coordinates or measured profiles: each holds one image, the analysis and processing groups are empty, and no OME ROI element is present, so the electrode footprints have to be found in the images. The plate (P1 to P3) and well (A1 to B3) of each image are given only by its subject id.

outcomes.note: The earlier criterion (claims/silkuniene-2025/001277.yaml) blocked the claim whenever its readings differ, and in both attempts the 15 individual values and the 3 means differ (earlier p 0.0020 to 0.050 against 0.012 to 0.18, here 0.0008 to 0.0058 against 0.048 to 0.165); the paper's claims file written under pilot-14 lets the author adopt the reading the paper best supports, and this attempt adopted the individual values. Both leave out the same two 600-ns wells, and the 1-mm readings differ (p 0.042 to 0.050 earlier, at most 0.0058 here) because this attempt centred 11 of the 15 wells, all five at 300 ns, on the YP spot where it found no reliable footprints, while the earlier one fitted a footprint square in every well.

The earlier criterion blocked the claim when its readings differ, and the claim also inherited the block of fig6d-longer-pulses-sharper-peak; there 900 against 300 ns was significant with contiguous ROIs (Bonferroni p 0.0053 to 0.0089) and not with 1-mm steps (0.077 to 0.131). The pilot-14 criterion gives partially reproduced when one comparison is significant, and here 900 against 300 ns is significant under every reading (0.0063 to 0.0118 over 2 comparisons), the 1-mm gap closed by the spot-centred wells (three spot-centred 900-ns wells at 1.60 to 1.81 mm against 1.85 mm for both footprint wells), while 600 against 300 ns is significant under no reading earlier and under one here.

The earlier attempt blocked the claim only because it depends on fig6d-longer-pulses-sharper-peak, which its criterion blocked; its own values met the criterion with contiguous ROIs (1.69 to 1.71 mm, 11.0 to 11.1%). This attempt's parent is reproduced, and its values, 1.688 to 1.767 mm and 11.03 to 11.55%, are essentially the same.

verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The first executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module cancan.py and the claims file, with the paper's full text (PMC12331426). The verifier read the session descriptions of all 329 assets on the archive and tested fit, gap_exceeds and find_array on synthetic inputs. It had no attempt record.

disagreements.reason: At 1 mm the gap rule fails (48.7 +/- 11.9 against 100 +/- 24.3); at 2 mm it holds. The criterion needs both. The notebook uses all 12, 11 and 11 YP wells where the paper reports n = 6 to 7; the August 2024 batch (7, 6, 7) matches the paper's n and was never run as a reading, and by batch the 1- and 2-mm centre values differ a lot.

Fitted to individual wells with the two 600-ns wells left out, all slopes are negative with p = 0.0008 to 0.0058; fitted to group means p = 0.048 to 0.165; with all 7 wells at 600 ns p is about 0.9. The two 600-ns wells P1-20240926-B2 and B3 were dropped after looking at their profiles; the paper gives no basis. B2's spot is 5.4 mm off the array centre, which supports leaving that one out. The other 5-of-7 subsets were not run.

Fitted to individual wells, CT26 p = 9.1e-4 (just under 0.001) and CHO p = 2e-11; fitted to group means p = 0.036 and 0.0015. The criterion needs every reading. CT26 at 2 bursts has n=6 from three dates where the paper reports 3 to 5, CHO 5 to 8 where it reports 4, so the selection could flip the result; no subset matching the paper's n was run.

Fitted to individual wells, CT26 p < 1e-6 and CHO p = 0.07 to 0.33, which meets the criterion. Fitted to group means, CT26 p = 0.0005 to 0.016, under 0.001 in only one combination. The CHO group-means p of 0.436 matches the paper's 0.44, which suggests the paper fitted group means.

verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The full executed notebook after the round-1 revision, with its conclusions and summary, the helper module cancan.py, the claims file, the attempt record and the README, with the paper's full text. The verifier checked each outcome and assumption, every sentence of the conclusions, summary, README and record notes against the printed outputs, and its round-1 points. Points not tied to one claim, and the responses: the summary said the FWHM claims are shown with the geometry difference taken out, when only fig6d-900ns-fwhm and fig7-sharpest-peak-one-burst are (the summary now names them); the 001277 "9 packets" finding rested on a fixed string in a print statement (the packet count is now parsed from every file and printed by pulse duration); the README's "about 45 GB" and "about 40 minutes" could not be checked (the notebook now prints the size of the files read, 46.7 GB, and the README gives the printed run time).

disagreements.reason: The criterion has no partial case, so the round-1 label of partially_reproduced was wrong. The O4 per-experiment assumption is reasonable. The well-selection assumption decides the outcome and is weak. B2 has an independent reason to be left out (its spot is 5.39 mm off the array centre); B3 does not: its spot is 0.33 mm from the centre and its centre value of 748 is within the 600-ns range, and its only printed anomaly is its FWHM of 5.49 mm, the quantity being tested. Every subset that keeps B3 gives p of 0.79 or more, and leaving out B2 alone (n = 6) was not run. "B2 and B3 are the only 0.2-MHz CANCAN wells without a central peak" is not supported: CT26 wells at 6 bursts have FWHM 5.51 to 8.05 and CHO wells at 1 burst 5.29 and 5.40, and "no central peak" for B3 rests on the montage image. Would record not_reproduced, unless B3's lack of a central peak is shown by a measure other than its FWHM.

Only the seven changes of outcome proposed after round 2 (fig3a-centre-enhanced, fig3bc-rate-suppresses-off-target, fig3-lorentzian-profile, fig4b-40-fold-ratio, fig6d-longer-pulses-sharper-peak, fig6d-600-900-differ-from-300 and fig7cf-fwhm-with-bursts), with the re-executed notebook, the claims file, the attempt record and the paper. disagreements.reason: Would give blocked (methods_underspecified). Cell 27. Under pooling (b) the claim holds in 24 of 24 readings. Under pooling (a) it holds in 40 of 48; 7 of the 8 left-side 7-mm readings fail, and one 6-mm reading (footprint iv) fails. The proposal adopts pooling (b) on the strength of the Fig. 4A legend. That legend describes the Fig. 4B near-electrode values. This claim cites Fig. 3B, whose legend says "Measurements in two diagonals were averaged and considered as one experiment", plotted from -x to x. Methods 2.5 says the same. So the paper supports pooling (a) for this claim, and (b) was picked after (a) had failed. Under pooling (a) the outcome also depends on the footprint; only footprint (i) with whole-mm ROIs passes, and the other 7 of 8 combinations fail. Under the claims-file rule that gives a block, as the author proposes for fig6d-600-900 and fig7cf. Every t-test gives p of 0.019 or less (all dates), and the 1-Hz group has n = 2, so the failures come from the graph rule applied to two wells. Nothing supports reproduced.

paper_notes.statement: Question for the authors. Were the regressions of Figs. 6D and 7B, C, E and F fitted to the individual experiments or to the group means? On individual experiments this attempt gets the reported significance (Fig. 6D p = 0.0008 to 0.0058; Fig. 7 CT26 p below 0.001); on group means the Fig. 7F CHO p (0.44) matches the paper but the CT26 and Fig. 6D slopes do not.

Question for the authors. Which five 600-ns wells form the Fig. 6 group, and what exposure did wells P1-20240926-B2 and B3 of 001277 receive? With them, the Fig. 6D trend is not significant, and of the 21 ways of choosing five of the seven 600-ns wells only leaving out these two gives a significant trend.

Question for the authors. Where were the ROIs placed along the diagonals, and which footprint gave the background? The centre to near-electrode ratios (Fig. 4B, Results 3.4) depend strongly on the background, as the near-electrode signal is close to it, and with the footprint at a fixed position in every well the Fig. 6D comparisons with 300 ns and the CHO slope of Fig. 7F change significance with the footprint.

entries.name: silkuniene-2025
entries.title: Remote focusing of electroporation by MHz pulse packets (Silkuniene et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Silkuniene, Silkunas, Pakhomova, Semenov and Pakhomov (2025) on dandisets 001047, 001276, 001277 and 001284, which hold whole-well images of cell monolayers stained with YO-PRO-1, propidium and Hoechst after CANCAN pulse exposures. It measures dye uptake along the diagonals of the four-electrode array for the raised-electrode and cell-killing series (001284), the pulse-duration series (001277) and the burst-number series (001276), with the packet-rate claims that its 1-Hz, 0.2-MHz and control wells allow. The 1-kHz and 10-kHz wells of Figures 3 and 4 are in none of the dandisets; 001047 holds images from a smaller array.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Silkuniene et al. (2025) from dandisets 001047, 001276, 001277 and 001284

entries.title: Remote focusing of electroporation by MHz pulse packets (Silkuniene et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Silkuniene, Silkunas, Pakhomova, Semenov and Pakhomov (2025) on dandiset 001277, which holds whole-well YO-PRO-1, Hoechst and propidium images of CT26 monolayers from the paper's pulse-duration experiment (Figure 6). It measures dye uptake along the diagonals of the four-electrode array, fits the Lorentzian of the Methods per well, and compares the central peak and its width across 300, 600 and 900 ns pulses, and the YP and propidium spots at 600 ns. The packet-rate, raised-electrode, burst-number and thermometry experiments are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Silkuniene et al. (2025) from dandiset 001277
